src: brief v2 §13a (bowling alley: fully playable lanes, the ball-return tunnel as a real squirrel route); brief addendum D4, D5 (eighteen lanes, the larger games room, the shops, the backstage behind the lanes); BUILD_PLAN §3.16-§3.17, W3c #15. Placement: the east commercial grass south of Bowl Lane (studs: the building x 1273.2..1449.8, z -351.2..-501.6; with the forecourt ramp, the rear alley and its fence x 1270..1452, z -338..-522). The origin, floor and yaw are the six-lane house's: lanes 1 to 6 did not move. The site slopes down to the east and to the rear: the front-west corner is cut up to 0.5 st into the ground (a terrain carve box) and the east wing stands on a plinth up to 7 st tall; the alley paving (floorY - 3.5) is above the highest ground behind the lanes. Units: STUDS (not HTML units). Route points are in the alley's local frame [X across the lanes, Y above the floor, D down the lane from the foul line]; tools/compile turns them into world points with Shared/Attractions/AlleyLayout.toWorld. The footprint is everything the alley bakes (the expansion planner keeps every venue site, street and pad out of it).

routes.name: bowling alley ball-return vent (lanes 1-2)
routes.note: Walk into the bent grille in the alley wall beside the trash cans: a trunk so the walk-in grab takes it; its end runs straight into the tunnel.

routes.name: bowling alley ball-return tunnel (lanes 1-2)
routes.note: Under the back of house, the pit and the whole lane, up the ball lift inside the hood and out of its mouth onto the rack (Space leaps at whoever is bowling). A bridge so it links back into the vent and leaps along the body's heading; visualOffset 0 keeps the body on the track.
